desc:
Rain and wind have made their mark on the rock face which blocks all passage
eastwards. In the process it has eroded the soft, reddish rock, causing plenty
of jagged shards to fall down onto this lower plain. A few bushes also grow here
close to the wall, apparently sheltered from the winds that freely roam these
forlorn fields.
name: Plains by the Escarpment

desc:
Quite a few rocks and boulders have fallen down off of the rock wall east of
here, this quite recently as damage to the various bushes and briars at the foot
of the escarpment is still fully discernible. What looks like a crevice in the
rock might actually be an opening into a cave. Westwards, the rolling plains
reach out towards the tree-dotted horizon.
name: Plains by the Escarpment

desc:
Growing next to an impressive, twenty feet tall rock wall, a few trees have
taken to clinging to the red and withered rock itself. On the ground, a few
ferns of a hardy kind, along with other plants and bushes, provide potential
cover for any number and species of animals. West, north and south of here, a
green and luscious plain reaches out, peppered here and there by dark green
clusters of trees.
name: Lower Plain

desc:
Boulders, rocks and a coarse, reddish kind of dust pepper the ground here,
obvious signs that the red-rock escarpment that lies east of here is slowly
retreating from the plain - probably due to the slow but relentless forces of
erosion: wind, rain and time. While passage east of here is hindered by the rock
wall, travel is still possible out onto the shrubby, undulating grasslands that
unfolds to the north, west and south from here.
name: Plain by an Escarpment

desc:
The looming cliff-wall north-east of here seemingly reaches out towards you,
poking a jagged pinnacle-crowned fist-like formation in the general direction of
the mighty Anduin river. Apart from this impressive geographical feature, the
plains that surround the escarpment provide a comparatively lush backdrop to the
stern, sterile ruggedness of the escarpment.
name: Curving Escarpment

desc:
Turning a sharp corner, an escarpment the height of a very large horse blocks
the way north and east. There has been considerable erosion of the cliff face;
thousands and thousands of reddish rock shards lie scattered on the ground,
interspersed with though green-greyish grass and waist-high juniper shrubs.
name: Bend in the Escarpment

desc:
A curious geological formation, this natural escarpment divides the plain into a
lower and a higher part. Northeast of here, a slightly curved, ramp-like path
leads up onto the higher section. Northwards, a reddish rock wall can be seen
rising out of the plain for miles and miles. Looking in a westerly direction,
one sees a fairly lush plain, interspersed with clumps of trees. Far in the
distance, a misty haze above the horizon reveals the location of the mighty
river Anduin.
name: At a Natural Ramp

desc:
The common juniper that grows here has the ability to take on a number of
interesting and bizarre shapes. Here, where the wind and the other elements can
torture the plants throughout their lives, the shrubs opt to stay low and close
to the ground; a fact that makes travel here somewhat difficult, whether mounted
or not.
name: Juniper Plains

desc:
Both rugged and desolate, this dusty plain offers little incentive for any
vegetation to grow. Only some tough, grey-green grass manages to survive here,
thriving in coloured patches - in stark contrast to the reddish soil that makes
out the ground on this part of the plains. To the west, a steep slope leads down
towards far more fertile plains.
name: Dusty Plain

desc:
At least one can be certain that these lonesome plains are not totally devoid of
life, as many creatures evidently use this spot as a watering spot. This is
quite incontestable, because tracks and droppings of many kinds of animals are
abundant. The lure of the location must be a slight depression in the reddish
plain, a basin-like pocket that serves as a reservoir of life-giving water,
something to be enjoyed by all kinds of local wildlife.
name: A Water Hole

desc:
Quite monotonously, these forlorn plains continue in all directions, only
occasionally livened up by the odd tree or bush. Upon closer inspection, this
particular site does actually bear the marks of recent occupation by one
traveller or another: the residues of an old campfire have been wedged in
between a dog-sized boulder and a tough-looking bush, and tiny splinters of wood
lie neatly piled next to it.
name: High Plain

desc:
A brutal-looking, jagged boulder tops this location - this is the very edge of
the escarpment that effectively cuts through this landscape, dividing it into a
lower and a higher part. The boulder itself is a red, weather-worn giant, and
would provide a great look-out if it only could be climbed. Almost hidden by the
edge of the boulder, traces of a recent campfire are strewn about.
name: Sharply Rising Plain

desc:
These stark and wind-pined plains reach an abrupt end west of here, where a
sheer cliff wall sharply dives down onto a lower plain. There are a few
scattered juniper bushes growing here, and they appear to keep well away from
the rock wall. Only tough, grey-green grass interspersed with a couple of
wind-eroded boulders dares to approach the vertical rift.
name: Escarpment on the Plain

desc:
One can see quite far to the west from here, since the plain below the
escarpment is considerably lower than the wind-pined patch up here. Only the
toughest of grasses and mosses can thrive here among all of the reddish boulders
and sharp, jagged rock shards that litter the ground. Looking in all directions
save west, one's view takes in a tough and desolate plain.
name: Escarpment on the Plain

desc:
Among these sombre plains, one would be more than surprised to find an abundant
flora and fauna. Thus, it is not a surprise that the same tough grass and the
same tough bushes that one can find in all other cardinal directions grow here.
Looking west one can discern a sudden drop in the plain, followed by more
plains. However, a misty haze obscures the horizon: evidence of the great Anduin
that brings life to the lower plains.
name: Austere Plain

desc:
Once upon a time, this was the place where this great, old grandfather of an oak
grew in perfect solitude. However, at some point lightning struck, splitting the
trunk in two and incinerating the whole tree. The new saplings that are trying
to replace the old behemoth have their work cut out for them, trying to grow on
these barren, unforgiving plains.
name: Plains by a Burned Tree

desc:
These undulating grasslands stretch in every direction. The plain is peppered by
trees and bushes of various kinds, giving the traveller the impression of an
untouched wilderness. One may wonder if the people that once inhabited these
lands abandoned them in order to seek out the company of fellow souls, or if
they were persuaded by some other kind of force.
name: High Plain

desc:
Most decidedly a great vantage point, this massive red sandstone boulder rises
some fifty feet from the lower plains. The verdant plains gently roll westwards
towards a faraway river. Access to this place is only granted from the air, or
through a severely difficult climb down unto the higher plain that lies on top
of the escarpment. Six consecutively smaller rocks have been piled upon each
other at the highest point as some kind of marker.
name: Top of a Huge Boulder

desc:
This big cavity in the cliff face has a dusty, hard-packed dirt floor strewn
with jagged rock shards and other debris. A few giant foot-prints can be found
in the dust, allowing the world to know that the cave indeed is inhabited by
some kind of creature. From the cave's ceiling hang strands of age-old spider
webs, webs that appear to have been disturbed quite recently. Westwards, a
twelve feet high crack allows passage to the outside world. It is also possible
to venture further east into the inky darkness of the inner parts of the cave.
name: Cave Entrance

desc:
Blackish stalactites reach down from the slightly domed ceiling of this dark
cave. The floor is littered with rocks and boulders, and the rough rock walls
lean into the room, defining the shape of the room into a neat 'T'. Towards the
south, the ground rises up to meet an equally lowering ceiling, enabling access
to what appears to be a continuation of the black grotto. Just north of here, a
portal-like formation allows passage into a pitch-black section of the cave.
name: Inner Cave

desc:
The stalactite-covered ceiling here is considerably lower than the cave part
north of here. The floor is littered with something that cannot be anything but
bat excrement, a fact that is effectively confirmed by the more than musty smell
in here. North of here, the cave appears to open up a bit, but it is hard to
tell in the prevalent darkness.
name: Dead End

desc:
By any measure, this cave is a complete and utter disaster zone. Gnawed bones,
dried up pieces of hide, skulls from animals and other creatures lie thrown
about in atrocious-looking piles. One would not have to think too long and hard
to find a plausible source for the absolutely rancid smell that permeates this
square, blackened cave room. A huge, jagged rock slab has been set up against
the eastern wall, blocking further passage in that direction. South of here, the
air appears to be easier to breathe.
name: Square Lair

desc:
The most prominent feature of this narrow alcove is the stench of rotting meat
that permeates everything in here. Spoils of war and strife are littered about
on the cave floor, mostly bones and skulls that have been crushed by merciless
hands not very long ago. The only exit from this unwholesome, dark hole lies to
the west, where a big opening leads into a big, nasty-smelling cave room.
name: Collapsed Tunnel

desc:
Only a few shrubs grow in the field here, the rest is consumed with long blades
of green grass. The grass has a variety of texture to it: some of the blades
have a refined texture, whereas others are very coarse. There are a few weeds
visible in the field as well, though they are not very tall in length, and the
grass hides the majority of them. However, along the northern edge of the field
the soil is exposed, giving off a red hue.
name: Grassy Field

desc:
A few shrubs are growing in the field, spread out wide apart from one another.
There are many leaves on each branch of the shrubs, oval in shape, with a dark
green colour to each. There are several weeds growing throughout the field, very
tall and of different shades of green. The grass is a mixture of green and brown
colour, with varying length. There is a slight incline upon the earth as the
field continues to the north.
name: Mixed Field

desc:
Shorter, fine grass grows among the very long, green blades of the field, making
it very thick in appearance. Tufts of brown grass are visible here and there,
stunted in their growth. Various types of weeds have mixed themselves into the
field among the grass here as well.
name: Mixed Field

desc:
Wild, brown grains are clearly dominating the grass in the field. The grain
stands very tall, though each one is quite slender. Slightly visible through the
thick, growing grain are light green blades of grass. The grass is very scant in
comparison to the wild grains. The field continues in all directions.
name: Wild Field of Grain

desc:
Grain flourishes in the field here among the grass. The grain plants are all
several feet high, with a slender stem of light brown. When the stem finally
reaches its tip, one can see the actual seeds of grain which are hanging, most
being cluttered tightly together. The grain seeds are a darker tone of brown
than the stem. A few soft green blades of grass have grown between some of the
grain.
name: Grainy Field

desc:
There is a large variety of grass growing in the field here. Some of the grass
is a soft shade of brown, other grass is fully green in colour. A few stems of
grain have also grown along the western side of the field, blending in with the
long blades of grass. There are also a few shrubs, low in height, which have
grown rather wide. Each shrub is thickly covered with leaves of an oval shape
upon their branches.
name: Grassy Field

desc:
Blended within the long blades of wild grass on the western side of the field
are a few stems of brown grain. The rest of the field is covered very thickly by
long blades of grass with different textures and colours to the blades. A few
weeds grow among the blades of grass, with diamond shaped leaves extending from
the stems. The weeds are a dark green, however, the stems of these weeds are a
much lighter green. A single shrub of a dark green colour grows within the field
as well.
name: Grassy Field

desc:
The field is quite thick, filled with grains and grass standing tall above the
soil. In all directions the field seems to be very expansive. There is an even
mixture of many different plants, all giving off their own natural essence to
the field. Along the ground, there are many decaying blades of grass, as well as
younger grass that has begun its growth.
name: Untamed Field

desc:
An even mixture of grain and lengthy grasses is covering most of the field.
Natural shades of green and brown from the plants in the field blend together so
well that only a few of the scrubby looking weeds stand out. The weeds have a
slight difference in tone to the grass surrounding them, making them a little
more noticeable.
name: Intermingled Field

desc:
There is a slight depression in the grassland here which inclines slowly on the
eastern side. The incline is gradual, not very steep even at its highest point.
The soil of the grassland is very soft and moist. Long blades of grass that have
grown here look very unhealthy, some are even frayed upon their edges. Along the
western edge of the grassland, where the ground becomes level, lies a dark hatch
that stands out as a landmark among the surroundings.
name: Marked Grassland

desc:
Many different coloured blades of grass consume the field here. However, there
are a few bushes that have grown within the field, with many oval-shaped leaves
of dark green upon each branch. An indentation through the centre of the field
reveals that something rather large has trampled the grass. It travels in a
straight line between the east and the west.
name: Lengthy Field

desc:
There are many blades of grass of several different colours growing wild here.
Many weeds grow exceedingly tall on the eastern edge of the field, where the
grass becomes very thick. A few dry shrubs are scattered around the field as
well. The leaves on the shrubs are small and oval in shape.
name: Rough Field

desc:
A large portion of the field here emits an essence of golden-brown. Almost every
blade is slender, tall in length and has a very refined texture to it. However,
at the northern end of the field, hints of green appear, blended in among the
rest of the golden-brown blades of grass. The difference in length of the green
blades is very noticeable, in comparison to those which are brown. The green
grass in the northern portion of the field is very short, whereas the
golden-brown seems to tower over the rest.
name: Golden-brown Field

desc:
The field is mixed with different coloured blades of grass. Some of the blades
are green, but the majority is a golden brown. There are a few places within the
field where the wild grass has been flattened, only to leave the once healthy
blades to decay, smashed into the soil. Two patches of bare soil are also
noticeable within the field.
name: Demolished Field

desc:
The majority of the blades of grass here are green in colour, with only a few
hints of brown at the southern portion of the grassland. Several shrubs have
grown far apart from one another, with branches filled with many dark green
coloured leaves. A slight depression can be seen in the grassland, dipping
gradually as it continues north.
name: Grassland

desc:
Along the northern portion of the grassland the grass is the more lush in
appearance, and more thickly grown as well. Towards the far southern edge of the
grassland, many stones lie upon the bare soil and it appears that the grass is
slowly coming to its end. The coarse grass that has grown in the southern area
of the grassland is very dry and brown in colour. Several weeds have sprouted in
random locations throughout the grassland and there are some large stones
embedded in the grass.
name: Blended Grassland

desc:
The field has an overall golden-brown hue to it, since every length of grass is
of that colour. The blades are all very long and slender, yet refined in
texture. The soil has been revealed from under the grass in a few locations,
though even that is a light shade of brown, blending into the colour of the
grass. Towards the south, a very bare plain can be noticed.
name: Golden-hued Field

desc:
Slender, tall blades of grass, all golden-brown in colour, grow in abundance
here in the field. On the south edge of the field the grass begins to diminish
until only bare soil remains. Even the bare soil is of a golden-brown hue. Some
stones are lying upon the earth where the grass has ceased to grow. The stones
are not very large and have a rough looking texture. There is a slight
depression throughout the centre of the field however, in a straight line, which
looks as though something rolled through in a north-south direction.
name: Golden-brown Field

desc:
Scattered around the plain are several large pits in the ground. Near some of
these pits are large rocks that appear as though somehow they were lifted out
from their deep bed of soil, for dirt and mud remain around the base of each
rock. Several of the pits have an odd shape to them, whereas a few of the pits
are extremely circular in shape.
name: Pitted Plain

desc:
Many rocks, stones and tiny pebbles of different shades of brown, grey and black
lie on the plain. They all have their own unique shape. Some of the rocks have a
rough texture to them and others are quite smooth. There are very few patches of
grass growing in this part of the plain, due to all the rocks which lie
scattered about, smothering the soil. The few grass patches that do exist,
appear to be very coarse; for the grass, there is a great struggle to stay alive
here, much less to thrive in growth. Towards the north of the plain, the
grassland has started. Its light, golden blades of grass meet the dry soil
there. The bare plain continues along to the east of it.
name: Rocky Plain

desc:
There are many large patches of rocky soil in the plain here. As it continues to
the north, the soil becomes hidden by lush grass. There are a few larger rocks
that the grass has encompassed, but most of the rocks sit in the dirt free from
grass. A few weeds also grow in the plain. The weeds have sprouted only where
the rocks have hindered the grass from growth; on the northern side of the plain
where there is more grass, there is not a single weed in sight. The brush from
the west is slowly beginning to expand into the plain here.
name: Bare Plain

desc:
The plain presents a desolate appearance. Rough grass of mixed green and brown
colours covers the ground in the middle of the plain. The soil is very dry and
light brown in colour. Eastward, across the plain, there are many rocks of
various sizes. There is a mixture of colour to the rocks, varying in shades of
brown, grey, and black.
name: Mixed Plain

desc:
Coarse grass is growing in bundles throughout the plain. There is a large area
where the bare soil is revealed with nothing growing in its vicinity. Two large
rocks have settled deep into the earth in the midst of the plain. They each have
a jagged texture, though they are also matching in a light brown colour. A few
weeds have grown up around the massive rocks.
name: Plain of Rocks

desc:
The brush slowly begins to fade here from the thick, brown plants that grow in
the west and south. There are several rocks on the ground, where the soil looks
very bare and dry. A few weeds growing here are dark green in their colour, with
many leaves sprouted from each stem. Fine, tiny hairs grow upon each leaf of the
weeds in the brush. The brush itself has several thorns that are spread apart on
each long, tangled stem.
name: Fading Brush

desc:
Quite a few pebbles, some larger stones, and clumps of soil lie across the dry
earth. Some tangled debris also remains scattered around the bare plain. From
the looks of the debris, it appears to have come from some kind of brush plants.
A few thorns are noticeable upon the tangled stems of the debris. Some brush can
be seen to the west, giving a brown hue to that direction.
name: Bare Plain near the Brush

desc:
There is not much to observe in the plain here, as the land appears very sterile
and dry. A few weeds have grown out from beneath the rough ground, along with
small patches of grass that looks as though each blade has been shredded. The
entire area gives off a brown essence, for even the few patches of grass are
parched due to the lack of shade.
name: Sterile Plain

desc:
Much of the soil is exposed on this plain. There are only a few patches of crisp
looking grass, scattered far apart from one another. These patches of grass only
show green at the base of each blade where it continues downward into the earth.
As each blade gets taller though, the green begins to fade into brown. A few
rocks, and clumps of loose soil, are noticeable on the eastern side of the
plain.
name: Barren Plain

desc:
The soil in the plain is not only bare, but very dry. Only a few slender weeds
have grown, although even these are not very tall in height. Large clumps of dry
soil lie upon the ground, easy to be mistaken for a large stone from a distance.
Along the western side of the plain, a few blades of coarse grass are visible.
name: In a Plain

desc:
The diminishing brush appears to come to an end here from the larger portion to
the north and west. Towards the east, the footing becomes extremely barren, with
various stones lying upon it. Several weeds have grown in between the thorny
stems of the brush, their hue of green making them very noticeable among all of
the brown colours. The weeds have tiny hairs covering their leaves, all of them
being very short and fine.
name: Diminished Brush

desc:
Vast thorns grow on the bushes with fine, sharpened edges to each thorn. The
branches are dark brown, the texture of each one alludes to the extreme dryness
that affects the area. A slight gap between some of the brush hints that some
kind of travel has gone through here before. The gap between the brush is very
narrow, only leading east or west. The brush is so dense towards the north and
south, that passage in either direction would impossible.
name: Thick Brush

desc:
Within this den are earthen walls made of natural clay. The den is not
necessarily large but has a rather decent amount of space inside. The clay walls
are all different shades of brown, some are even red, and have a clumpy, natural
look. The den overall has a circular shape to it, with the base having a very
dark colour of brown. Debris is scattered upon the ground of the den, along with
long, dried up blades of grass.
name: Earthy Den

desc:
The walls forming the tunnel are of natural materials. Consisting of a lot of
packed mud, roots, and other plant-like materials, they appear to hold quite
well. A lot of moisture has built up in the tunnel making it very humid. The
space here is very narrow, and becomes even more so near far end, making it
difficult to pass through.
name: Muggy Tunnel

desc:
The narrow, muggy tunnel opens widely into a rather large, old dwelling place of
some sort. The underground dwelling at one time must have been the home to a
small being, as much of the remaining debris appears to once have been made for
a creature of much smaller stature if compared to Men. Though there is a large
portion of stone that was used as a ceiling, it has now been collapsed for what
appears to be a long time. Even with this fallen stone, there is still a
sufficient amount of space within the enclosed tunnel. Between the fallen stones
near the southern corners hang many webs, some weaved in unique patterns.
name: Collapsed End

desc:
This underground chamber's walls were made of natural stones and pieces of rock.
The stones and pieces of rock were firmly placed into the earthen walls with
some kind of black material in between the stones to seal them. The stones were
placed tightly together, even though each is oddly shaped. The floor of the
chamber was laid with several pieces of flat, black slate. Between each piece of
slate there are cracks that were left unfilled with sealant; now water has built
up in between them from all the moisture in the earth. On the eastern wall,
there are two torches braced between stones by small metal brackets. Below the
torches is a scarlet coloured canvas concealing the wall. However, on the
northern wall a lever of golden colour is visible.
name: Underground Chamber

desc:
Within this chamber there are four slender pillars, which are providing support
for keeping a black sheet of slate, used as the ceiling, in its proper place.
The flooring is of the same slate that was used for the ceiling, though there
are many carved grooves upon the surface. The four walls were made of many
natural stones pressed tightly together into the earth, with a black sealant to
fill the tiny spaces between them. In the centre of the chamber, there is a
large, black orb.
name: Inner Chamber

desc:
A sharp drop in the plain blocks all passage westwards, as a twenty feet high
cliff wall plunges down onto the grassy plain beneath it. Along the ridge, a few
scattered bushes are kept low in stature by the winds that must blow here most
of the time. South of here one can notice the beginnings of a downward slope.
name: Escarpment on the Plain

desc:
This patch of ground dips below the surrounding plains. The borders of the
depression resemble the shape of a bowl. On the eastern slope some shelves of
sand and rock border a small crack, just large enough to fit through.
name: Sunken Patch of Ground

desc:
To the larger creatures of Arda the height of the grass might be a mere
hindrance. However, to a hobbit, dwarf and to other smaller creatures the height
of the grass holds a real danger of getting lost as the tall stalks go on
forever as an entangled maze. One can only pick a direction and hope that it
leads out of the sea of grass.
name: Tall Grass

desc:
To the north and west the ruins of a stone wall can be seen, but this particular
area is virtually devoid of anything but grass. If it were not for the
occasional landmarks of small trees and stones, it would be quite possible to
get lost in this endless sea of vegetation.
name: Tall Grass

desc:
A section of an ancient wall has not withstood the test of time. Fallen stones
lay all about, partially sunken into the earth at the foot of the structure.
Moss has begun to grow on part of the wall that still stands. A path is worn
between the standing sections showing use by different creatures to come and go
as they please.
name: Break in a Wall

desc:
The grass here grows far thicker than almost any other nearby region. Some
cattails have also grown up towards the northern part, adding variety to the
mostly bare scenery.
name: Lush Plains

desc:
In contrast to the rest of the plains, this area has some plant-life other than
grasses. A few hardy shrubs sprout from the ground here, providing a slight
change of scenery from the seemingly endless plains about them. Nestled among
the shrubs is a pool of water with a rather muddy bank. Pawprints in the mud
suggest that this is a frequent spot for the denizens of these lands to stop and
take a drink.
name: At a Waterhole

desc:
Standing alone, tall and forlorn, is a single dead tree. Its branches have been
stripped away by harsh weather. Over time part of the trunk has split off to
rest beside its standing portion. To the west, past the plains, the remains of a
stone wall can be seen.
name: By a Dead Tree

desc:
The native grasses have made themselves quite at home around an ancient stone
wall. The wall itself, however, seems to have seen better days. Stones are
missing along the top and side, leaving small niches for dirt and water to
collect. A few plants have taken advantage of this, growing out of the ancient
structure itself.
name: By a Crumbling Wall

desc:
The ground looks very unsteady, sand and dirt being ready to shift upon any
pressure laid upon the ground. Parts of the land have already caved in, giving
way to dangerous sinkholes. Especially to the west the ground looks so difficult
that it prevents travelling into that direction.
name: Uneven Plains

desc:
Flat land stretches out in all directions, studded with occasional skinny trees.
The land is very green, tall grass covers most of the plains rippling with every
breeze that passes. The dark shadow of Mirkwood can be seen far to the east.
name: Rolling Plains

desc:
Old, dry bones litter the ground and have killed some of the grass around them,
leaving small, bare spots in the plains. Around the mound of gnawed bones some
pawprints, new and old, can be seen leading off to different directions.
name: Rolling Plains

desc:
Debris from the forest just to the west is prevalent here, adding some variety
to the characteristics of a typical grass field: large branches emerge above the
grassline, twisting among the briars and weeds. To the south, a crumbling stone
wall cuts across the plains.
name: Brushy Plains
